title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree The Impossibility Of Producing Its Like In View Of Source Addressee And Purpose

questions.question: According to the passage, what three things help show the worth of any speech?
questions.answer: Its speaker, its audience, and its purpose.

questions.question: Why does the passage say no speech can truly match the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Because it comes from the Lord of all creation, addresses the greatest messenger, and explains the deepest truths and purposes of life and the universe.

questions.question: Who is described as the speaker of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: The Sustainer of all worlds and Creator of the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the style of this divine speech?
questions.answer: It is not copied, fake, or forced.

questions.question: Who is the Qur'an primarily addressed to in the passage?
questions.answer: The Messenger sent on behalf of all people, and even all beings.

questions.question: How is the faith of the one addressed by the Qur'an described?
questions.answer: It is presented as the strongest and widest in reach.

questions.question: What effect did that great faith have in history, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It led to the rise of mighty Islam and raised its bearer to a very high rank.

questions.question: What kinds of topics does the Qur'an explain, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It explains success in this life and the next, why the universe was created, and the divine purposes within it.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur'an shows about the universe?
questions.answer: It displays the universe from every side and teaches it as the Maker knows it.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the universe to things like a map, a clock, or a house?
questions.answer: To show that the Qur'an presents the universe in an organized, understandable way.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the Qur'an’s way of explaining the universe?
questions.answer: That producing anything equal to it is impossible for people.

questions.question: What have many highly intelligent scholars done with the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They wrote detailed commentaries to explain its qualities, meanings, and hidden signs.

questions.question: How large were some of those commentaries?
questions.answer: Some were thirty, forty, or even seventy volumes long.

questions.question: What do these many commentaries try to show?
questions.answer: They try to prove the Qur'an’s many special features, subtle meanings, and signs related to unseen matters.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur described in relation to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: As a collection whose parts each prove a different quality or fine point of the Qur'an with strong arguments.

questions.question: What kinds of subjects are said to be drawn from the Qur'an in those writings?
questions.answer: Things such as signs about modern inventions, meaningful patterns in its words, and verses giving news about unseen matters.

questions.question: What final proof do all these studies together provide?
questions.answer: They confirm that the Qur'an has no equal, is miraculous, and speaks from the unseen by the knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: What basic rule about speech is given at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: To judge speech well, you need to know who said it, who it is for, and why it was said.

questions.question: Based on that rule, why is the Qur'an presented as above all other speech?
questions.answer: Its source, audience, and purpose are all greater than any human speech.

questions.question: What is special about the source of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It comes from the Lord and Creator of everything.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says the Qur'an has no sign of imitation?
questions.answer: It is original and not made by copying others.

questions.question: How wide is the audience of the Qur'an, as described here?
questions.answer: It is directed through the Messenger to all humanity and even to all beings.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the rank of the Messenger who received it?
questions.answer: He is the most honored and well-known among people and was raised to an extremely lofty closeness.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the rise of Islam?
questions.answer: To show the power and reach of the Messenger’s belief.

questions.question: What main goals of human life does the Qur'an address?
questions.answer: It teaches about well-being in this world and in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What does the Qur'an explain about the universe besides its creation?
questions.answer: It explains the outcomes of creation and the divine wisdom within it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the belief of the Messenger?
questions.answer: As the highest and broadest faith, holding all the truths of Islam.

questions.question: In what way does the Qur'an teach about the universe like its Maker?
questions.answer: It presents the universe completely and meaningfully, as only its Maker fully can.

questions.question: What does the passage say about making something like the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It says reaching its level is not possible.

questions.question: What is the role of major commentaries on the Qur'an in this passage?
questions.answer: They serve as evidence that learned scholars found endless depths to explain in it.

questions.question: What does the great number and size of those books suggest?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an contains vast meanings and layers that require deep study.

questions.question: What is one special role given to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It is said to prove distinct truths and subtle features of the Qur'an one by one.

questions.question: What do the examples from the Risale-i Nur have in common?
questions.answer: They all point to different signs of the Qur'an’s wisdom, order, and miraculous nature.

questions.question: What overall message does the passage give about the Qur'an through these examples?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an is unmatched, wondrous, and a true divine message connected to the unseen.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person know in order to understand how great a speech is?
questions.answer: The one who spoke it, the people it addresses, and the reason it was spoken.

questions.question: How does this idea lead to the claim that the Qur'an is beyond comparison?
questions.answer: Because every one of those three parts is at the highest level in the Qur'an.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the One who speaks the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He is the Lord of all worlds and the Creator of the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say is missing from the Qur'an’s speech style?
questions.answer: Any trace of copying or artificial effort.

questions.question: To whom is the Qur'an delivered first, according to this passage?
questions.answer: To the Messenger who represents all people and all creatures.

questions.question: What does the passage tell us about that Messenger’s place among humanity?
questions.answer: He is described as the most famous and most honored of people.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Messenger’s faith with the spread of Islam?
questions.answer: It says the strength and reach of his faith brought forth powerful Islam.

questions.question: What subjects of guidance are included in the Qur'an according to the passage?
questions.answer: Human happiness in both lives, the purpose of creation, and the divine meanings within the universe.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of how the Qur'an presents the universe?
questions.answer: It presents it clearly and from all sides, like a fully explained design.

questions.question: What inference can be made from that description about human ability?
questions.answer: Human beings cannot produce a book equal to such a complete divine explanation.

questions.question: What have many brilliant scholars contributed concerning the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They have written careful explanations showing its many meanings, secrets, and signs.

questions.question: What does the passage say these scholars used in their studies?
questions.answer: Evidence and reasoned arguments.

questions.question: What kinds of things are said to be found in the Qur'an by these scholars?
questions.answer: Fine points, special qualities, high meanings, and hints about hidden realities.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur used as an example?
questions.answer: As a work whose many sections each uncover and prove a different aspect of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What final judgment does the passage make after giving all this evidence?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an is unique, miraculous, and the speech of the One who knows the unseen.

questions.question: What three questions does the passage say help us recognize the quality of a statement?
questions.answer: Who said it, who receives it, and what goal it serves.

questions.question: How does the passage apply that rule to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It argues that the Qur'an’s source, audience, and purpose are so great that nothing can equal it.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the source of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: The Lord of all existence and Creator of the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say about whether the Qur'an sounds man-made?
questions.answer: It says it has no sign of being copied or artificially put together.

questions.question: Who is the receiver of the Qur'an in this passage?
questions.answer: The Messenger who was sent for all people and all beings.

questions.question: How is this Messenger described in terms of reputation and honor?
questions.answer: As the best known and most honored among mankind.

questions.question: What shows the greatness of his faith according to the passage?
questions.answer: Its strength and scope brought forth Islam and lifted him to an exalted spiritual rank.

questions.question: What does the Qur'an teach about human life?
questions.answer: It teaches what leads to good in this world and in the next life.

questions.question: What does it teach about the universe?
questions.answer: It explains why it was created and what divine wisdom is within it.

questions.question: Why are objects like a house, a clock, and a map mentioned?
questions.answer: To help the reader picture how the Qur'an lays out the universe in an ordered and understandable way.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from the Qur'an’s complete explanation of reality?
questions.answer: That nobody can produce another book at its level.

questions.question: What do the many long commentaries on the Qur'an reveal?
questions.answer: They reveal that scholars saw countless depths and details in it worth proving and explaining.

questions.question: What kinds of features do those commentaries discuss?
questions.answer: They discuss its special qualities, hidden meanings, mysteries, and signs about unseen matters.

questions.question: What is said about the parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Each section is said to establish one truth or one light from the Qur'an.

questions.question: Give one kind of topic those sections are said to explore.
questions.answer: They explore things like signs related to inventions, meaningful word order, or reports about the unseen.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention so many examples of scholarly study?
questions.answer: To show that careful study keeps uncovering proofs of the Qur'an’s depth and miracle.

questions.question: What final conclusion is stamped by all these proofs?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an is without equal, miraculous, and a divine word bringing knowledge from the unseen into this world.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what is said to determine the rank of words?
questions.answer: The identity of the speaker, the audience, and the aim of the message.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this standard proves the Qur'an is unmatched?
questions.answer: Because its speaker is Allah, its audience is the noblest messenger for all beings, and its purpose covers the greatest truths.

questions.question: What title for Allah is highlighted to show the greatness of the Qur'an’s source?
questions.answer: That He is the Lord of all worlds and the Creator of the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the Qur'an shows no sign of imitation?
questions.answer: That it is fully original and not a product of human effort.

questions.question: How broad is the mission of the person who receives the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He is sent in the name of all people, even all beings.

questions.question: What does the passage say his faith accomplished?
questions.answer: It gave rise to a powerful civilization of Islam and lifted him to a very high nearness.

questions.question: What areas of guidance does the Qur'an provide according to the passage?
questions.answer: It guides about success in both worlds, the results of creation, and the purposes placed in the universe.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the belief carried by the Messenger?
questions.answer: As the broadest and highest faith, containing all Islamic truths.

questions.question: What is the purpose of comparing the universe to a map, a clock, and a house?
questions.answer: To show that the Qur'an explains creation in a clear, structured, and useful way.

questions.question: What claim follows from the Qur'an’s ability to explain the universe like this?
questions.answer: That no one can bring forth anything truly equal to it.

questions.question: What kind of people are said to have written many explanations of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Careful, knowledgeable scholars with great intelligence.

questions.question: What do these scholars prove through their writings?
questions.answer: They prove the Qur'an’s many qualities, subtle points, secrets, elevated meanings, and signs.

questions.question: What is important about the length of some of these writings?
questions.answer: Their great length shows how much deep material the Qur'an contains.

questions.question: What special place does the passage give to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It presents it as a strong body of work in which each part proves a particular aspect of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What do the examples from the Risale-i Nur tell us about the Qur'an’s content?
questions.answer: That it contains layered meanings, ordered wording, and signs pointing to realities people later notice more clearly.

questions.question: How do all these scholarly efforts function in the passage?
questions.answer: They act like a seal confirming the Qur'an’s uniqueness and truth.

questions.question: What is the final description given of the Qur'an at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as an unmatched miracle and as the speech of the One who knows the unseen.

questions.question: What does the passage say we must consider when judging the excellence of speech?
questions.answer: We must consider its source, its audience, and its purpose.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about the Qur'an after applying that rule?
questions.answer: That nothing similar to it can be reached.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an’s source so exalted in the passage?
questions.answer: It comes from the One who sustains all worlds and created the entire universe.

questions.question: How is the Qur'an’s manner of speech described in relation to imitation?
questions.answer: It is described as free from borrowed or artificial wording.

questions.question: According to the passage, who receives this divine address?
questions.answer: The Messenger sent on behalf of all people and all beings.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Messenger’s standing?
questions.answer: As the most celebrated and highly honored human being.

questions.question: What evidence from history is used to show the power of his faith?
questions.answer: The emergence of strong Islam through that faith.

questions.question: What are the main themes the Qur'an explains in this passage?
questions.answer: It explains human happiness in both worlds, the purpose of creation, and the divine meanings in the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the scope of the Messenger’s belief?
questions.answer: It was the most complete and far-reaching belief, holding all Islamic truths.

questions.question: How does the passage say the Qur'an presents the universe?
questions.answer: It presents it from every angle in a way only its Maker can fully teach.

questions.question: What does that suggest about attempts to imitate the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Such attempts cannot succeed because people cannot reach its level.

questions.question: What kind of work have many scholars done on the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They have written detailed commentaries supported by proof and reasoning.

questions.question: What do these commentaries uncover in the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Countless special features, subtle meanings, mysteries, and indications of unseen matters.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention commentaries of many volumes?
questions.answer: To show the richness and depth of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What is said about each section of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Each one demonstrates a certain truth or ray from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What broad lesson comes from the examples listed from the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an contains precise order, deep wisdom, and signs that go beyond ordinary human speech.

questions.question: What overall seal do all these explanations and proofs place on the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They confirm that it is unequaled, miraculous, and the word of the Knower of the unseen.
